angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 710,310 km at 148.51 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.7335 +/- 0.0182 mas (same row, RUWE 1.07): 148.51 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.021 +/- 0.038 solar radii from Dattilo et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-6109 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..318D/abstract): 710,310 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.03 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Dattilo et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-6109 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..318D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5660 +/- 50 K from Dattilo et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6109 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..318D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dattilo et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6109 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..318D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-6109.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.433, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
